newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama Congress passes new Panama Canal law.
newsitem.headline: Panama Congress passes new Panama Canal law.

text.p: Panama's Congress has passed a new law to govern operations of the Panama Canal under Panamian control next century, Foreign Minister Ricardo Arias said on Thursday.
"It's a message to the world that Panama is assuming control of the Panama Canal in a responsible manner," Arias told reporters. "We must manage the canal efficiently and effectively," he said.

The law, passed unanimously late Wednesday by the 72-member Congress, will create the Panama Canal Authority and replace the Panama Canal Commission (PCC) and all U.S. laws affecting the canal's operations, Arias said.
It will take effect once Panama takes over control of the canal from the United States on Dec. 31, 1999.
The law denies the canal's 9,000-strong labour force the right to strike and creates an 11-member board of directors, a congressional spokeswoman said.
President Ernesto Perez Balladares will this year appoint a chairman and directors to staggered terms of three to nine years, she said.
